public_rationale: The factual core holds: OpenAI backed an Illinois proposal containing the described conditional liability shield. The assessment does not endorse the accusation of lying. OpenAI disavowed the shield before Marcus published, while acknowledging its earlier support for the bill. Altman’s 2023 comments also left the allocation of liability open. Those qualifications materially weaken the rhetorical comparison without making the earlier support disappear.
limitations: This outcome applies to the legislative-support proposition, not the allegation of deceit.
The shield was conditional and covered defined catastrophic harms.
Primary Illinois records were inaccessible, so attributed reporting supplies the legislative facts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI recently supported an Illinois state law that would shield AI labs from liability in cases where AI models are used to cause serious societal harms, which Marcus calls pretty much the opposite of what Altman told Senator Durbin in his 2023 testimony.

statement.excerpt: His company did however recently support state law in Illinois that “would shield AI labs from liability in cases where AI models are used to cause serious societal harms, such as death or serious injury of 100 or more people or at least $1 billion in property damage”– pretty much the opposite of what he said to Senator Durbin in his deceitful, lie-filled testimony.
statement.document_title: Maybe Section 230 doesn’t shield AI companies from liability, after all

from_speaker: recently support state law in Illinois
would shield AI labs from liability
death or serious injury of 100 or more people
at least $1 billion in property damage
our_interpretation: The checkable core is OpenAI’s support for an Illinois proposal containing the described liability protection.
Because the sentence says “would,” read “state law” as proposed legislation rather than a claim that it was enacted.
Read “recently” as the current legislative year through publication.
The comparison with testimony is an evaluative characterization. Support for a conditional liability shield alone cannot establish knowingly false testimony.
The dollar amount is a statutory harm threshold, not a claim about OpenAI’s finances.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish that OpenAI supported an Illinois bill containing conditional protection from liability for the specified catastrophic harms.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the attributed support did not occur, or that the supported proposal lacked the described protection.

evidence.locator: Paragraph immediately following the description of SB3444

evidence.explanation: The article reports the stated 100-person and $1 billion thresholds. Protection required published safety documentation and excluded intentional or reckless causation; covered harms involved weapons or specified autonomous criminal conduct. Reporting substitutes for inaccessible legislative records.

evidence.locator: The Big Story; paragraph quoting OpenAI’s written testimony
evidence.explanation: Before Marcus’s post, OpenAI expressly disavowed the shield and backed a different bill. This qualifies the implied continuing policy position but does not erase its earlier support for SB3444.

evidence.explanation: Altman called for a new framework and discussed responsibility shared among developers, intermediaries, and users. This does not commit him to unlimited liability; it is historical comparison material outside the target period.
